correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), the closed-neighborhood activity inequalities follow by counting the \(2n\) external votes plus self. Allowed flips cannot decrease cut size. The cut is multi-affine in the three part occupancies and has exact maximum \(2n^2\), with all maximizers two unanimously opposite parts and one free part. From every state an explicit allowed path of at most \(2n\) flips reaches this set. Six pair-labelled hypercube faces meet cyclically and are connected; uniform reversibility follows from neutral flips. Six corner configurations are counted twice, giving exactly \(6(2^n-1)\). Two boundary configurations of each face have \(n\) outgoing switches apiece, yielding conditional escape probability \(2/(3\cdot2^n)\); the stationary domination argument proves \(t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)>\lfloor3\cdot2^n/4\rfloor\). Independent direct SCC enumeration for \(1\le n\le4\) and constructive/exact-boundary enumeration for \(1\le n\le6\) pass. Finite checks support but are not substituted for the all-\(n\) proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected foundational 2010 primary text supplies the stochastic rule and general monotone potential, not the six-hypercube recurrent geometry, exact labelled count or conditional escape flux for balanced tripartite graphs. The inspected 2019 primary work requires strict conflict-reducing switches and studies stabilization duration, so neutral motion and mixing within a nonabsorbing class are outside its model. The closest accessible scientific-record hits and existing related claims have different graphs or updating rules. Explicit proof steps add a motivated, non-implied graph-family invariant. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The model is a natural dense \(2n\)-regular antiferromagnetic network. The complete recurrent class classification is a nontrivial structural invariant: six high-dimensional hypercubes glued at corners, rather than frozen maximal cuts. The exact stationary flux quantitatively separates frequent local flips (limiting probability \(1/3\)) from exponentially slow global mixing despite a unique recurrent class and uniformly short directed paths to it. This is a mathematically motivated metastability effect on a graph family unrelated to earlier sparse hub bottlenecks.
